sn45.8:1.2: See note on [sn12.2:1.2]() for a discussion of “analysis” discourses.
sn45.8:3.1: “View” (_diṭṭhi_, Sanskrit _dṛṣṭi_) is “seeing” and hence a term for “understanding” (Aitareya Upaniṣad 3.2). In Buddhism it means a particular way of seeing or perspective, a theory or view through which one makes sense of the world. By itself it is neutral, although “views” in plural sometimes stands for the thicket of wrong views.
sn45.8:4.1: _Saṅkappa_ may be rendered with “thought” ([sn14.8:3.3](), [mn60:24.2]()), “intention” ([mn41:14.3]()), or perhaps “resolve”. In Rig Veda 10.164.5 it is the “evil intent” wished upon those who we hate.
